title: Americans urged to exercise increased caution ‘worldwide’
byline: The US State Department has issued an updated caution to Americans across the world due to the ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

title: Sri Lanka Police flag fake social media message; Urge public caution
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has issued a clarification regarding a message circulating on social media that has been falsely attributed to the Sri Lanka Police.

title: Bus fare revision proposal to be presented to Cabinet today
byline: The proposal to increase bus fares is scheduled to be presented to the Cabinet today (23).

title: Showers expected in certain parts of the island
byline: Showers or thundershowers may occur at several places in Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces and in Galle, Matara and Nuwara-Eliya districts after 2.00 pm, today (23), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Asian stock markets tumble
byline: Major Asian stock markets fell sharply on Monday after the US and Iran threatened to intensify hostilities as the war enters its fourth week.

title: Macron calls for ‘‘halt to attacks on energy facilities’‘ in talks with Saudi Crown Prince
byline: French Prime Minister Emmanuel Macron on Monday held talks with Mohammed bin Salman, Crown Prince of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

title: Increased heat exposure can raise concerns over child dehydration - Health Officials
byline: Health officials have urged parents to pay special attention to protecting children from dehydration amid the prevailing extreme heat conditions.

title: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un reappointed as president of state affairs
byline: North Korea has re-elected Kim Jong Un as president of state affairs, state media reported on Monday (Mar 23).

title: Several private bus operators suspend services amid delay in fare revision
byline: Severe queues were reported at major bus terminals this morning (23) after several private bus associations withdrew from operations pending a formal revision of bus fares.

title: Saudi Aramco cuts oil supply to Asia for second month in April
byline: Saudi Aramco, the world’s top oil exporter, has cut crude supply to Asian buyers for a second month in April, two sources with knowledge of the matter said on Monday, after the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran disrupted trade via the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Dollar rises as escalating Middle East war spurs haven demand
byline: The dollar rose on Monday as escalating retaliatory threats in the Middle East conflict curbed risk appetite and lifted demand for safe-haven assets.

title: ADB Chief arrives in Sri Lanka on official visit
byline: The President of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Masato Kanda arrived in Sri Lanka on an official visit this morning (23).

title: Vehicle parking fee collection in Colombo resumes today – CMC
byline: The Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) has resumed the collection of vehicle parking fees across its jurisdiction from today (23).

title: World faces worst energy crisis in decades, IEA chief warns
byline: The war in the Middle East could plunge the world into its worst energy crisis in decades, International Energy Agency (IEA) Executive Director Fatih Birol warned on Monday, describing the situation as ‘‘very severe.’’

title: Air Canada Express jet hits ground vehicle, closing New York’s LaGuardia airport
byline: An Air Canada Express regional jet collided with a ground vehicle upon landing at New York’s LaGuardia airport on Monday evening, according to flight tracking website Flightradar24, in an incident that closed the airport.

title: Bus services disrupted in several areas; NTC proposes over 10% fare increase
byline: A shortage of bus services has been reported in several areas today (23), despite a limited number of buses being in operation, according to Director General of the National Transport Commission (NTC), Dr. Nilan Miranda.

title: Private buses withdrawn from services, not on strike – Gemunu
byline: The President of the Lanka Private Bus Owners’ Association (LPBOA), Gemunu Wijeratne, stated that the decision by private bus operators to withdraw from services today (23) is not a strike action.

title: US attack on ‘IRIS Dena’ near Sri Lanka a violation of humanitarian law - Iranian Ambassador
byline: At a special press conference held at the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Colombo, Iranian Ambassador Dr. Alireza Delkhosh made a series of serious allegations regarding recent developments involving Iran and the United States.

title: Rear Adm. Princely Liyanage completes 48-hour treadmill endurance, qualifies for three Guinness World Records
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy proudly announces that Rear Admiral Princely Liyanage (Retd) has etched his name in the annals of global endurance by qualifying for three Guinness World Records on a manual treadmill.

title: Iran expresses readiness to support Sri Lanka with essential supplies, including oil
byline: At a press conference held at the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Colombo, Iranian Ambassador Dr. Alireza Delkhosh reiterated Iran’s commitment to its bilateral relationship with Sri Lanka and emphasized continued cooperation between the two countries.

title: Iran threatens to attack Mideast electrical plants powering US bases
byline: As U.S. President Donald Trump’s deadline on opening the Strait of Hormuz approaches, Iran on Monday threatened to attack Mideast electrical plants powering American military bases.

title: FR petition against Suresh Sallay’s arrest to be considered in Sept.
byline: The Supreme Court has ordered that a Fundamental Rights (FR) petition challenging the arrest and detention of the former Head of the State Intelligence Service, Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay, under the Prevention of Terrorism Act, be taken up for consideration on September 25, 2026.

title: Ex-Minister Arjuna Ranatunga and brother indicted over corruption case
byline: Former Minister Arjuna Ranatunga and former Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) Dhammika Ranatunga have been served indictments before the Colombo High Court today (23) on a corruption charge.

title: Food and travel costs expected to surge amid prolonged conflict, analyst says
byline: Consumers around the world can expect to pay more for groceries and travel as the energy crisis triggered by US-Israel war with Iran drags on, an analyst told CNN.

title: All services at Dept. of Registration of Persons suspended tomorrow due to system failure
byline: Services at the head office and regional offices of the Department of Registration of Persons have been affected following an unexpected breakdown in its computer system.

title: UK sees no evidence of Iran targeting Britain, says PM Starmer
byline: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said on Monday there had been no assessment that mainland Britain was being targeted by Iran.

title: President urges citizens to conserve energy during peak hours
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake instructed the officials to take all possible measures to safeguard the country’s energy conservation by raising public awareness on the prudent use of energy during the peak consumption period between 6.00 p.m. to 10.00 p.m., while ensuring the active participation of the public in these efforts.

title: China launches 10 satellites aboard Smart Dragon 3 carrier rocket from Sea platform
byline: China successfully launched 10 satellites into orbit late on Sunday, using the Jielong 3 (Smart Dragon 3) carrier rocket that lifted off from a mobile launch platform in the Yellow Sea off the coast of Haiyang in Shandong province, state media reported.

title: Sri Lanka and Australia hold talks to strengthen bilateral ties
byline: A meeting between the Chief of Staff to the President, Prabath Chandrakeerthi, and the Australian High Commissioner, Matthew Duckworth, was held at the Presidential Secretariat this morning (23).

title: Sri Lanka’s inflation decreases to 1.6% in February 2026
byline: The overall rate of inflation, as measured by the National Consumer Price Index (NCPI), has decreased to 1.6% in February 2026, compared to 2.4% in January 2026, according to the latest data released by the Department of Census and Statistics.

title: Powdered milk and wheat flour prices to remain unchanged until New Year
byline: Prices of imported powdered milk and wheat flour in the country will not be increased under any circumstances, the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development has announced.

title: Global shipping could reroute around South Africa for the rest of 2026, expert warns
byline: Shipping companies may avoid passing through the Middle East and opt for longer routes around the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa, following security concerns in the region, an expert said.

title: Iran says there is “no dialogue between Tehran and Washington”
byline: Iran has denied any dialogue with Washington, dismissing President Donald Trump’s claims as an attempt to lower energy prices and buy time for military plans, several Iranian state-affiliated media outlets reported citing the foreign ministry.

title: Donald Trump postpones military strikes on Iranian power plants
byline: President Donald Trump said on Monday the U.S. has had good and productive conversations with Iran and he will order the military to postpone any military strikes against Iranian power plants ⁠and energy infrastructure for five days.

title: Sri Lankan delegation meets Indian Lok Sabha Speaker
byline: A Sri Lankan parliamentary delegation led by Parliamentarian S. M. Marikkar called on Indian Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at Parliament House, underlining efforts to strengthen bilateral ties between the two nations.

title: Russia calls for ‘political’ settlement over Iran as Trump says US talking to Tehran
byline: Russia on Monday (Mar 23) called for a “political and diplomatic” settlement to the Middle East war just as US President Donald Trump claimed that Washington and Tehran had held talks on ending the conflict.

title: Private bus operators to resume normal operations tomorrow after bus fare hike – LPBOA
byline: The Lankan Private Bus Owners’ Association (LPBOA) says it is satisfied with the new bus fares approved by the National Transport Commission (NTC).

title: Bus fares increased by 12.19%; Minimum fare at Rs. 30
byline: The bus fares will be increased by 12.19 percent from midnight today (23), Cabinet Spokesman Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa has stated.

title: Strait of Hormuz will be “open very soon” and US and Iran would jointly control it: Trump
byline: President Donald Trump told CNN Monday that the Strait of Hormuz will be “open very soon,” adding he’d like to see the vital shipping route under joint US and Iranian control.

title: UAE official blasts Arab and Muslim countries for failing to support Gulf states under attack
byline: A top official from the United Arab Emirates has criticized “major” Arab and Islamic nations for failing to support Gulf Arab countries in “times of hardship.”

title: Oil falls over 13% on Trump postponing military strikes on Iran energy infrastructure
byline: Oil prices plummeted Monday after US President Donald Trump suggested that ongoing talks between the United States and Iran could end the war.

title: PM Harini chairs meeting to review proposal to establish National Nursing University
byline: A discussion to review the current progress of the special committee appointed under the government’s policy proposals to establish a National Nursing University aimed at elevating the nursing profession in Sri Lanka to degree level was held at the Prime Minister’s Office today (23).

title: Price of bread up by Rs. 10 while prices of other bakery products also increased
byline: The price of a 450-gram loaf of bread will be increased by Rs. 10 with effect from midnight today (23), according to the All Ceylon Bakery Owners’ Association.

title: Badulla hospital staff save man after iron rod pierces through body
byline: The medical staff attached to the Badulla Hospital have succeeded in saving the life of an individual who suffered a horrific accident, in which an iron rod pierced through his abdomen and came out from his back.

title: Suspended Sri Lanka Customs officer arrested by Bribery Commission
byline: A suspended Sri Lanka Customs officer has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) following an inquiry.

title: Three-wheeler fares increased
byline: Three-wheeler fares have also been increased in line with the recent fuel price revision announced by the government.

title: Oman working toward safe passage of vessels through Strait of Hormuz
byline: Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said today that Oman is “working intensively” toward the safe passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz while highlighting the economic turmoil caused by the war.

title: 2 dead, 41 injured after plane and firetruck collide at LaGuardia Airport
byline: The pilot and co-pilot were killed and dozens of people injured at New York’s La Guardia Airport late Sunday night when an arriving Air Canada Express plane and firetruck collided on a runway, officials said.

title: Dimuth Bhashitha Atapattu appointed as new DG of Data Protection Authority
byline: Dimuth Bhashitha Atapattu, an officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service (SLAS), has been appointed as the Director General of the Data Protection Authority (DPA).

title: Iran Defence Council issues Strait of Hormuz order for ‘non-hostile countries’
byline: Iran’s high-level security body Defence Council has said in a statement that the ‘‘only way for non-hostile countries’‘ to pass through Strait of Hormuz is ‘‘coordination with Iran."
